q.instruction: 밑줄 친 단어의 영영풀이로 적절하지 않은 것은?
q.passage: Denotative ⓐ<u>meaning</u> 6.1 If we had to think of a list of features or criteria that defined both the ⓑ<u>words</u> ⓒ<u>woman</u> and lady, one might suggest that they include being human, female and adult. A definition based on these lines would be the DENOTATIVE MEANING of the two words. But there must be more to meaning than this, since we know that there is a difference between these two words – we know they can be used to mean ⓓ<u>different</u> things. Consider these words placed in the context of the sentences below. She’s only ⓔ<u>thirteen</u>, but she’s a woman already She’s only thirteen, but she’s a lady already Connotations What differences in meaning – what different associations or CONNOTATIONS – do the words have? One way in which dictionaries try to give us clues about usage is by providing quotations where the word is used.
